data.name: Shivashankar
data.gender_notes: Shivashankar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Shivashankar is a name derived from the Sanskrit words ‘Shiva’ and ‘Shankar’. Shiva is the name of the Hindu god of destruction, time, and creation. Shankar means the lord of the mountain or god of mountains. Therefore, Shivashankar can be interpreted as a powerful and strong name, invoking the blessings of the god Shiva.
data.spiritual_meaning: Shivashankar is a name that symbolizes the divine power and strength of Lord Shiva. It is a name that is believed to bring blessings, protection, and success in various aspects of life.
data.etymology: Shivashankar belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Shiva + God of Mountain.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shivashankar total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Shivashankar is rooted in ancient Hindu mythology and carries significant cultural importance. Shiva is known as the destroyer of evil and the purifier of the universe. He is a significant deity in Hinduism, and his worship is widespread across India and beyond. The name Shivashankar acknowledges and pays homage to his divine power. Likewise, Shankar as the god of mountains represents the strength and stability of nature. Mountains are considered sacred in Hinduism and are often associated with spiritual growth and self-realization. The fusion of these two powerful concepts in a name serves to remind us of the vast and intricate tapestry of Hindu traditions and myths.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper level, Shivashankar as a name signifies the union of the divine and the material world. Shiva's destructive power represents a necessary force for purification and renewal in the universe. The mountain, symbolizing stability and strength, also has spiritual significance as it is oftentimes seen as a place for spiritual retreat and communion with higher powers. The combination of Shiva and Shankar in this name serves as a constant reminder of the power of the divine to transform and bring a sense of balance and stability to life. It is a testament to the profound spiritual beliefs that have influenced the Hindu culture for centuries.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shivashankar: The name Shivashankar is a combination of two powerful Hindu deities - Shiva and Shankar. Shiva represents the destroyer of all impurities and negativity, while Shankar symbolizes Lord of the Universe and absolute consciousness. Together, Shivashankar signifies the supreme power that destroys all obstacles on the path to enlightenment and ultimate union with the divine.

historical_references.reference: Shivashankar was a title given to Shiva during the Chalukya dynasty of Karnataka, India. It is believed that King Vijayaditya (1086-1100 CE) built the Shivashankar Temple in honor of this deity.
historical_references.context: Chalukya dynasty, Karnataka, India, Shivashankar Temple

historical_references.reference: Shankaracharya Shivabhutendra was a Hindu philosopher, theologian, and saint, who lived during the 17th century in southern India. He wrote extensively on Shiva philosophy and is considered a major figure in the history of Shivism. Shivashankar is a combination of his personal name Shivabhutendra and the title Shankar, which refers to Lord Shiva.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Shivashankar' is associated with Lord Shiva, who is considered the deity of destruction, creation, and regeneration in Hinduism. In modern contexts, this name is frequently used on various digital platforms to discuss devotional content, cultural practices, and spiritual beliefs. On Twitter, users share their personal experiences and beliefs, while on Instagram, visual content like images and videos of temples, rituals, and idols are popular. On YouTube, religious hymns and prayers are posted and watched by millions. Overall, the name 'Shivashankar' reflects the deep cultural and spiritual significance of Lord Shiva in Hinduism and continues to be a trending topic in modern digital discourse.
